title: Collecting the Divine Shard
text_md:
# Chapter 1: Collecting the Divine Shard

[narrator] The ash did not fall; it hovered, a suspended gray fog that tasted of old iron and burnt hair. It settled on everything, coating the stone steps of the ruined temple in a fine, dry powder that resisted washing away. There was no rot here, Kaelen noted, looking at the skeletal remains of a cart horse half-buried in the drift. The flesh had simply desiccated, pulled dry by the absence of the god’s breath, leaving only bone and leather that cracked at the touch. Kaelen Vord adjusted the strap of his satchel. The weight of the Ledger against his hip was a constant, dull pressure, a reminder of the authority he carried and the exhaustion it demanded. He was tired. Not the kind of tired that sleep fixes, but the deep, marrow-level fatigue of a man who has been awake for too long, carrying a burden that grows heavier with every mile. He stood before the iron doors of the Temple of Oaths. They were sealed with three sigils, each one a knot of golden light that pulsed with a slow, rhythmic beat. The third seal was cracked. A hairline fracture ran down the center, leaking a faint, sickly vapor. "The third one is giving way," Kaelen said, his voice rough from disuse. Sera stepped out from the shadow of a collapsed pillar, her boots making no sound on the ash. She held a short sword in her right hand, the blade sheathed in worn leather, and her eyes were fixed on the horizon, scanning for threats that hadn't arrived yet. "It’s always giving way," Sera said. She didn’t look at him. "That’s why we’re here. To stop it from falling completely before the debt is collected." Kaelen ran a gloved hand over the first seal. The gold light flared, warm against his palm. "The contract is for ten gold pieces, Sera. Ten gold. For a loaf of bread and a night’s shelter in the village of Oakhaven. Three hundred years ago." Sera finally looked at him, her expression unreadable. "And the interest?" "Compounded daily," Kaelen replied. He pulled the Ledger from his satchel. The book was bound in black leather that felt like cold skin, the pages thick and yellowed. He opened it to the marked page. The ink was still wet, shimmering slightly.

[SYSTEM] Debt Entry: #8940-B Creditor: Kaelen Vord (Proxy of the Deceased) Debtor: The Village Council of Oakhaven (Dissolved, 142 P.A.) Principal: 10 Gold Accrued Interest: 4,200 Gold Status: Unpaid. Seal Integrity: 68%.

[narrator] "Four thousand two hundred gold," Kaelen read aloud, his tone flat. "For a loaf of bread." Sera snorted. "The economy of the dead is weird. Let’s just get it done. I don’t like standing in the open when the seals are active. It makes my skin itch." Kaelen closed the book and slung it back over his shoulder. He looked at the iron doors. The handle was shaped like a clenched fist. He placed his hand on it. The metal was icy cold. "I need to verify the lineage of the current representative," Kaelen said. "The village is gone. The town is gone. The city is gone. What’s left?" "The ash," Sera said. "And the echoes. If there’s a soul bound to this place, it’ll be in the ash. You have to find it. You have to ask it. And it has to pay." Kaelen nodded. This was the process. It was not heroic. It was clerical. He was a collector, not a warrior. He didn’t swing swords; he swung paperwork. But sometimes, the paperwork required a bit of persuasion. He pushed the door. It groaned, the sound echoing through the empty nave of the temple. Inside, the air was still and thick with dust. The pews were rotted away, leaving only the stone floor, which was covered in a layer of ash so deep it looked like snow. Kaelen walked down the center aisle, his boots crunching softly. Sera followed, her hand resting on the hilt of her sword. "Stay close," she said. "The dead don’t like to be disturbed." Kaelen ignored her. He knew the rules. The dead didn’t care. Only the debts mattered. At the altar, a faint glow emanated from the ash. Kaelen approached it, the Ledger growing heavier in his hand. He knelt, brushing the ash away with his hands. Beneath the gray drift, he found a small, bone-white figure, no larger than a doll. It was made of compacted ash and memory, a remnant of a priest who had served the god before the god died. "Speak," Kaelen said. The figure twitched. A voice, dry as parchment, whispered from it. *"...payment..."* Kaelen opened the Ledger. He turned to the page for Debt #8940-B. "The Village Council of Oakhaven owes me four thousand two hundred gold pieces. The debt is due. The seal is cracking. You have until the seal breaks to pay, or I will take the value from your remains." The ash figure trembled. *"We... we have no gold. The mines dried up. The trade routes closed. The god left, and the world forgot us."* Kaelen sighed. He didn’t like this part. It was always the same story. The world moved on. The debt remained. "Then I will take what you have," Kaelen said. He reached into the Ledger and pulled out a silver coin. It was small, stamped with the face of the dead god. "This is a token of the god’s authority. It is worth one year of service in the afterlife. Do you agree to transfer three thousand two hundred years of service to settle the debt?" The ash figure shook its head violently. *"No! I am bound to the temple! I cannot leave!"* Kaelen frowned. He flipped through the pages of the Ledger, searching for a loophole, a clause, anything that would allow him to collect without breaking the binding. The book was thick, the text dense and legalistic. He found a section on 'Eminent Domain'. "The temple is property of the god," Kaelen said. "Since the god is dead, the property is in probate. I am the executor. Therefore, I have the right to seize the assets." The ash figure recoiled. *"That is... that is theft!"* "It is collection," Kaelen corrected. "And you are insolvent. So, I will take the asset directly." He reached into the ash figure and pulled out a small, glowing shard. It was a piece of the temple’s foundation, imbued with the residual magic of the god’s presence. It pulsed with a soft, blue light.

[SYSTEM] Loot Acquired: Shard of Divine Foundation (Quality: Rare) Value: 1,500 Gold Note: Can be sold to a collector of divine remnants.

[narrator] "Three thousand two hundred years of service," Kaelen said, looking at the shard. "This is worth half of that. I will have to find the other half elsewhere. But this will buy us time." The ash figure faded, its form dissolving back into the ash. The debt was not paid, but it was acknowledged. The seal on the door outside pulsed, the crack widening slightly. Kaelen stood up, brushing the ash from his knees. "Let’s go." Sera was waiting by the door, her sword drawn. "Did you get it?" "I got a shard," Kaelen said. "It’s not enough, but it’s something. We need to find another debtor. Someone with gold." Sera lowered her sword. "There’s a caravan coming in from the east. They’re carrying spices and silks. If we intercept them, we can extract a fee for 'safe passage' through the Vale." Kaelen looked at her. "You want to rob them?" "I want to collect a debt," Sera said. "The Vale is dangerous. We are providing a service. It’s fair." Kaelen shrugged. "Fine. But we need to be quick. The seal is cracking. We don’t have much time." They stepped out of the temple, back into the gray fog. The wind was picking up, swirling the ash into spirals that looked like dancing spirits. In the distance, the rumble of wheels could be heard. The caravan was coming. Kaelen adjusted his satchel. He felt the weight of the Ledger, the weight of the debts, the weight of the god’s dead authority. He was tired. But he was also efficient. And efficiency was what the world needed.

[SYSTEM] Quest Update: The Ashen Ledger Current Objective: Break 3 Seals Seal 1: Broken. Seal 2: Cracked. Seal 3: Cracking. Progress: 1/3 Seals Broken. XP Gained: 50 Level Up: Kaelen Vord is now Level 2. New Skill Unlocked: Authority (Passive) - You may enforce contracts on non-sentient entities without resistance.

[narrator] Kaelen didn’t notice the notification. He was too busy watching the caravan approach, calculating the distance, the speed, the potential yield. Sera checked her sword, her face set in a grim line. The ash swirled around them, waiting for the next transaction.
